claims.claim: Swish containment is exactly a multiplicity-respecting directed-cycle problem.
claims.evidence: After fixing one allowed transformation for each selected physical card and directing its hoop position to its ball position, the Swish condition says that every used vertex has indegree and outdegree exactly one. Every finite nonempty component is therefore a directed simple cycle, and the cards in any component form a contained Swish. Conversely, the distinct physical cards realizing a directed simple cycle contribute exactly one hoop and one ball at each cycle vertex. Requiring a separate physical copy for every used arc gives precisely the stated multiplicity constraint.
claims.witness: For any realizable opposite pair p→q and q→p, the two distinct cards form a two-card Swish; neither singleton does. More generally, any cycle component of a transformed Swish is itself the required contained Swish.
claims.search_method: Direct proof from the Swish degree conditions, supplemented by exact labeled-cycle regression checks on the reconstructed 4×3 type system.

claims.claim: A no-swish collection contains at most 20 distinct transformation types, and this is sharp.
claims.evidence: Exact orbit generation gives four position orbits of sizes 4,2,4,2 and 36 card types. Eight types are internal, distributed 3,1,3,1; the other 28 form 14 reversal pairs. Both types in a cross reversal pair realize a two-cycle, so a no-swish support uses at most 14 cross types. On either four-position orbit, the three internal types are the three perfect matchings of K4 and one card from each realizes a directed triangle, giving bounds 2 and 2. Each two-position orbit has only one internal type. Hence the support bound is 14+2+1+2+1=20. The stated 20-type construction was checked cycle-free, proving sharpness.
claims.witness: Order A={(1,1),(1,3),(4,1),(4,3)} < B={(1,2),(4,2)} < C={(2,1),(2,3),(3,1),(3,3)} < D={(2,2),(3,2)}. Take the 14 cross types directed forward and one copy of each internal type represented by (1,1)→(1,3), (1,1)→(4,1), (1,2)→(4,2), (2,1)→(2,3), (2,1)→(3,1), and (2,2)→(3,2). Cross arcs strictly increase orbit rank, while the internal selections contain no cycle.
claims.search_method: Generated all symmetry orbits exactly, checked every reversal-pair two-cycle and every internal local obstruction, derived the counting bound, and ran an exact labeled-cycle search on the 20-type witness.

claims.claim: Unless all eight internal types are duplicated, the usual once-or-twice interpretation of the 60-card deck already yields a 29-card no-swish subset.
claims.evidence: Under the explicitly stated once-or-twice interpretation, 60 cards over 36 present types means exactly 24 types are doubled. If d≤7 internal types are doubled, the eight internal types contribute 8+d≤15 cards, leaving 52−d≥45 cross cards. Across the 24 total orders of the four position orbits, each directed cross type is forward in exactly 12 orders. Thus the integer average forward count is at least 45/2, so some order contains at least 23 forward cross cards. Adding one copy of each of the six cycle-free internal types gives at least 29 cards. Every cross arc strictly raises orbit rank, so no directed cycle can use one; the internal part is also cycle-free. Deleting extras preserves the no-swish property.
claims.witness: Choose an orbit order attaining at least 23 forward physical cross cards and add the six internal representatives from claim 1. This produces a no-swish subcollection of size at least 29 whenever at most seven of the eight internal types are doubled.
claims.search_method: Exact integer double counting over all 24 orbit orders; the checker verified forward incidence 12 for every cross type and the ceiling bound for every possible doubled-internal count d=0,...,7.

claims.claim: The authorized input omits information essential to deciding the exact commercial-deck target.
claims.evidence: The authorized source states that the deck has 60 physical cards and 36 symmetry types and that a 28-card no-swish subset exists, but supplies neither a physical-card list nor a 36-entry multiplicity vector. The omission is logically decisive because two once-or-twice decks satisfying all those aggregates have different target answers. In Deck X, double all eight internal types and both directions in eight cross reversal pairs. Local two-cycle and triangle bounds give at most 6 internal plus 16 cards from the eight doubled pairs plus 6 from the remaining pairs, totaling 28; a forward construction attains 28. In Deck Y, double nine forward cross types, all 14 reverse cross types, and one internal type. Both copies of the nine chosen forward types, one copy of the other five forward types, and the six safe internal cards form a verified 29-card no-swish set. Each model has 36 present types, 24 doubled types, 60 cards, and a 28-card no-swish subset.
claims.witness: Deck X has exact maximum 28, while Deck Y has the explicit 29-card forward-orbit witness. The checker constructs both capacity vectors deterministically and verifies their counts, Deck X's upper bound and attaining witness, and Deck Y's cycle-free 29-card witness.
claims.search_method: Inspected only the authorized source fields and relevant deck statements, then constructed and checked two exact aggregate-compatible multiplicity vectors using exhaustive local capacity enumeration and exact labeled-cycle search.
